newsitem.title: HUNGARY: NATO-Russia pact dispels fears - Hungary.
newsitem.headline: NATO-Russia pact dispels fears - Hungary.

text.p: Hungary welcomed a historic NATO-Russia security pact signed on Tuesday in Paris, saying the agreement dispelled concerns of NATO hopefuls about possible second-class membership.

"We especially welcome the fact that the document does not contain any commitment on NATO's part that would restrict the rights of new entrants, or would lead to some form of 'second-class' membership," Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi told a news conference.
NATO leaders and Russian President Boris Yeltsin signed the Founding Act on Mutual Relations designed to bind Russia into efforts to create a new European security order.

"This is a compromise that does not hurt the medium or long-term interests of either side," Szentivanyi said, adding that Hungary had always given "due consideration" to Russia's justified security interests.
NATO is expected to issue the first invitations to prospective new members -- expected to be Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic -- at a summit in the Spanish capital Madrid in July.
